events.text_en: Vưu Chước Kim of Thối Tinh Môn quarrels with his head at the forge. Cát Lưu Quang breaks Vưu's hammer and sends him down the mountain.

Vưu Chước Kim strikes the blade Three Years' Tax with lightning, and it sings; he strikes an ingot of Thiên Ngoại iron, and it does not. What he says of the iron is kept by the head, by Vưu and by the quench-keeper Bàng Lãnh Tôi.
Cát Lưu Quang lends his second son, Cát Thối Phong, to Thiên Xu Tông as the armourer of its seat.
Nhạc Bá Chùy, who forged Trầm Sa Kích, is refused leave to draw it from the barrow on Chiết Kích Nguyên, and dies that winter.
The last of the sky-iron seam at Thiên Ngoại Khoáng is forged into blades for the Pivot's war; below it the mine gives ordinary mountain iron, and the gate goes on calling it star iron.
